title: A Comparative Assessment of Advanced Fenton‐Based Processes: Methylene Blue Oxidation Using Zero‐Valent Iron
content:
Advanced zero-valent iron–based Fenton systems achieved 93%–99% methylene blue removal within 30 min, with hydroxyl radicals identified as the dominant reactive species.


ABSTRACT

This study presents a comparative assessment of several advanced Fenton-based processes for the degradation of methylene blue (MB) in aqueous solution using spontaneous corrosion of metallic iron in an acidic medium in the presence of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). Six advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) were initially tested; based on degradation efficiency, the two most effective processes were selected for further investigation, namely, the photocatalytic-ZVI-Fenton (PCF) and photocatalytic Galvano-Fenton 2 (PCGF2) processes. For PCF, MB degradation reached 89.38% and 99.28% after 5 and 30 min, respectively, at an initial concentration of 10 ppm. At 50 ppm, it reached 61.06% after 5 min and 99.24% after 30 min. For PCGF2, the degradation rates were 93.95% and 99.32% at 5 ppm, and 65.68% and 99.48% at 50 ppm. A detailed parametric study was then conducted to examine the influence of key operating parameters—the pH, the nature of catalysts, namely titanium dioxide (TiO2) and tungsten trioxide (WO3), and the effect of Sodium chloride (NaCl) and tert-butanol present in the electrolyte. The results showed that the use of TiO2 as a catalyst is significantly more effective than that of WO3. MB degradation efficiency decreased with WO3, reaching 65.56% and 70.90%, respectively, as well as 16.73% and 67.04% for 10 ppm and 50 ppm MB solutions in the PCF and PCGF2 processes. Furthermore, the results showed that degradation efficiency is higher in an acidic environment (pH = 3) than in an alkaline environment (pH = 10), whereas the addition of NaCl led to a reduction in the performance of the processes studied. Similarly, the presence of tert-butanol inhibited the degradation of the dye, confirming the major role of hydroxyl radicals (HO•) in the oxidation process. The results obtained highlight the potential of ZVI-Fenton processes for the effective treatment of dye-containing wastewater.
